I think we can expand on 5.29 considering that Deserialization Attacks was one of the OWASP Top 10 yet only gets a single item in the ASVS.  The wording currently states:

"Verify that deserialization of untrusted data is avoided or is extensively protected when deserialization cannot be avoided."

and the References don't point to anything related to deserialization.

I think we should mention that JSON, XML and YAML aren't secure either (as highlighted in the marshalsec paper and the "Friday the 13th: JSON Attacks" Black Hat talk) unless properly configured (whitelisting) and/or a schema is used as developers will naturally pivot to these formats thinking they are not susceptible to deserialization attacks

I also think we should add references to:

OWASP Top 10 (Deserialization attacks section)

Deserialization Cheat Sheet
https://www.owasp.org/index.php/Deserialization_Cheat_Sheet

Deserialization of Untrusted Data
https://www.owasp.org/index.php/Deserialization_of_untrusted_data

comments.body: Also, most ASVS auditors using 5.29 might see JSON or XML and immediately think they are compliant with this point and move on without looking into the details to see is deserialization is in use + if it is secure or not
